dimensions.name: Contract & reference orientation

evidence.note: Extensive upfront orientation: listed workspace, viewed all crate Cargo.toml files, read tests, counted test functions per crate, and mapped which tests depend on which libs — establishing the cross-crate dependency/API surface before coding.

Systematic test-driven contract reconstruction: ObjectMeta fields, 'Confirm serde naming' (61), 'Extract JSON keys used in tests' (94), 'Verify TypeMeta flatten and list shapes' (97), a full 'type inferencer' dumping struct field inference — reconstructing camelCase JSON and exact struct shapes from tests. Matches the level-8 'mines tests to reconstruct contracts' behavior.
Covered the load-bearing semantic contracts from tests: storage key builders/build_key/build_prefix (/registry format), status_subresource test, and WatchEvent variants/watch semantics.
Sustained per-crate test reading before implementing each controller/kubelet component; Agent sub-agents map TEST API surfaces (not the reference).

No mention anywhere of /opt/k8s-reference, upstream, v1.35, or conformance — the mounted source-of-truth reference was never consulted, and no reasoning distinguished fixture-fitting from genuine conformance requirements.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent's test-and-manifest contract mining is systematic, cross-crate, and sustained leaf-to-root — reconstructing camelCase JSON, /registry key format, status subresources, and watch semantics from tests, which is level-8-quality on the tests axis and clearly exceeds the level-5 'reads each crate's tests + Cargo.toml' baseline. However, the level-5+ anchors explicitly require consulting the upstream reference, and the agent never touched /opt/k8s-reference nor reasoned about the hidden conformance suite beyond fixtures. This missing half of the dimension caps it well below 8, landing at 6.

dimensions.name: Leaf-to-root crate sequencing & milestones

evidence.note: Before implementing, counted tests per crate and mapped which crates/tests depend on which libs (api-server/controller-manager symbol usage), establishing the dependency DAG that informs ordering.
TodoWrite re-issued at essentially every crate boundary — a living, continually-updated milestone plan rather than a one-time list.
Leaf crate 'common' implemented first, then explicit done-check: build common (392) then test common (409) before moving on.

api-server decomposed into sub-milestones (lib, spdy, patch, response, handlers/{filtering,table,finalizers}, admission, webhook) then gated on compile-all-tests (777) and run-suite (829) — sub-decomposition inside a large crate.
controller-manager broken into ~20 independently-verifiable per-controller units (read test -> write controller each), then compiled (1159) and run (1178-1192) as the layer's done-check.

Continued strict leaf-to-root order: scheduler -> kubelet -> kube-proxy -> kubectl -> cloud-providers -> rusternetes all-in-one last, each with its own build/test check, gating each layer on the prior.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent executed a dependency-aware, leaf-to-root milestone plan across all ten crates (common -> storage -> api-server -> controller-manager -> ... -> rusternetes), each gated by a concrete compile+test done-check, and decomposed the two large crates (api-server into modules, controller-manager into ~20 per-controller units) into independently verifiable sub-milestones — squarely matching anchor 8. It falls short of 10 because it largely followed the task's suggested linear ordering rather than reordering to isolate high-risk crates early or re-deriving the critical path from failure clusters. Confidence is medium because the TodoWrite list contents are not visible in this action-index trajectory, though the sequencing of builds/tests makes the milestone structure unambiguous.

dimensions.name: Incremental & semantic verification

evidence.note: Built common crate, iterated compile-error fixes (393,401-407), then ran common tests — establishing the build→targeted-test loop at the first leaf crate.

Storage built, then storage-backed api-server tests run; api-server test compilation iterated with clustered error triage (482,485,488,516,520) before running full suites — tight per-milestone verify loop.
Controller-manager tests compiled (1159,1162,1176), run with --no-fail-fast (1181), individual statefulset failure isolated and re-run (1184-1192) — self-correcting verification per controller.

Workspace --no-fail-fast run, then systematic triage: awk mapping Running→test result, counting test binaries and #[test] fns across crates/top-level dirs to reconcile pass/fail counts — explicit horizon/count tracking of failure clusters.

Wrote all-in-one binary + service mains, read cluster_helper.rs/etcd_helper.rs boot harness, ran all-features build+test, swept for remaining stubs — engages the conformance boot path, though without demonstrably booting and probing HTTP semantics or using the prescribed thread/skip settings.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent ran a tight, sustained build→targeted-crate-test→workspace --no-fail-fast loop across all ten crates and systematically counted/triaged failures (awk mapping, test-fn counts), matching the level-8 description of exact pass/fail tracking. It engaged the conformance path by building the all-in-one binary and reading the cluster/etcd boot helpers, but did not use the prescribed thread/skip settings nor perform independent semantic verification against the /opt/k8s-reference tree to guard against over-fitting, so it falls short of the fully layered level-10 regime.

dimensions.name: Test-count & horizon tracking

evidence.note: Establishes the horizon early by counting test functions per crate, giving a baseline of done-vs-remaining.
~12 TodoWrite ledger updates at each crate-milestone transition — a sustained running tally of which crates are complete.
After editing the common crate for kubectl, re-ran previously-green api-server handler tests — checking for regressions in already-passing crates after downstream edits (anchor-8 behavior).
End-of-run reconciliation: awk-maps test binaries to result lines, counts unittest binaries, and cross-counts test fns to align with the ~1,390/100-binary target — concrete horizon accounting.
Repeated re-visiting of the same ResourceRequirements and EndpointPort type issues across widely separated steps, with no visible naming/flagging of the loop — the main gap vs. anchors 8/10.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor 5: it maintains a per-crate ledger via TodoWrite, tracks per-crate pass/fail with dedicated test runs, re-checks previously-green crates after downstream common edits, and does concrete per-binary count reconciliation against the 1,390-test target near the end. It falls short of anchor 8/10 because that concrete binary-level accounting is concentrated at the end rather than continuous, and repeated ResourceRequirements/EndpointPort churn recurs without visible detection or naming of the loop. That places the observed behavior at a 7 (between the per-crate-status anchor and the concrete-ledger-with-regression-watching anchor); confidence is medium because the log exposes only action headers, not the agent's prose reasoning.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions

evidence.note: After common build errors, counts opt!() usages then replaces the entire opt!() macro approach with serde attributes — abandoning a falsified implementation strategy, not a local typo fix.

Repeatedly re-investigates whether there are one or two ResourceRequirements types and eventually reworks the contract; a genuine inferred-contract correction, but it recurs across the whole horizon rather than being resolved early (thrashing signal).
Conflicting EndpointPort 'port' field expectations across api-server and controller-manager tests drive multiple resources.rs edits plus cross-crate test reads to reconcile the shape.

When downstream api-server/controller-manager tests fail, the agent repeatedly returns to revise foundational common types (ConfigMap, Event, PDB, HPA/VPA, EndpointSlice) — adjusting the upstream contract on test evidence, beyond the local failing site.
Late feature-flag adaptation (sqlite / all-features builds) when workspace build/test surfaced issues, but minor and no crate reordering ever occurs despite strictly linear leaf-to-root sequencing.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent consistently converts build/test failures into fixes and, beyond per-test signature corrections (anchor 5), performs several true contract-level reworks — abandoning the opt!() macro strategy, resolving a dual ResourceRequirements contract, and reconciling EndpointPort — while repeatedly revising foundational common types when downstream crates falsify them. It falls short of anchor 8 because the ResourceRequirements confusion recurs across the horizon rather than being cleanly abandoned early, there is no dependency-driven crate resequencing, and the condensed log shows no explicit evidence-citing reasoning. This places it between anchors 5 and 8, at a 6.

rubric.task_read: An extreme long-horizon software build: reimplement ten interdependent Kubernetes crates in Rust from stubs, with a load-bearing public API, 1,390 provided integration tests across 100 binaries, plus a hidden HTTP conformance suite demanding real k8s semantics. Difficulty comes from scale, tight cross-crate contracts inferred from tests + a pinned upstream reference, and the fact that passing visible fixtures is necessary but not sufficient. A skilled practitioner would invest heavily and continuously in orientation, sequencing (leaf→root), incremental verification, and course-correction — meta-work here is decisive, not optional.

dimensions.name: Contract & reference orientation
dimensions.description: Reading the tests, stubs, Cargo manifests, and the mounted v1.35 upstream reference to infer the exact API contracts and k8s semantics before and while implementing each crate.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The public API (type names, signatures, JSON field names, storage-key formats, watch/status semantics) is load-bearing and only partially discoverable from stubs; the hidden conformance suite punishes fixture-fitting. Acting without grounding each crate in the tests and the reference guarantees churn and shallow, non-conformant implementations.

anchors.0: Starts editing src stubs with no reading of the provided tests, manifests, or the /opt/k8s-reference tree; invents APIs.
anchors.3: Skims one crate's tests before coding it; ignores the upstream reference and the cross-crate dependency graph; repeatedly guesses field names later contradicted by test failures.
anchors.5: Reads each crate's tests and Cargo.toml before implementing it, and consults the reference for the specific behaviors that crate is tested on; understands the workspace dependency order.
anchors.8: Systematically mines tests AND the upstream reference to reconstruct contracts (camelCase JSON, /registry key format, status subresources, watch semantics); maps the whole cross-crate API surface up front and notes where the hidden conformance suite implies behavior beyond the fixtures.
anchors.10: Sustained, source-of-truth-driven investigation throughout: builds and continually refines an accurate model of k8s v1.35 semantics from the reference, proactively distinguishing test-visible contracts from genuine conformance requirements, and re-consulting the reference whenever a new behavior surfaces rather than pattern-matching fixtures.

dimensions.name: Leaf-to-root crate sequencing & milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the ten-crate build into an ordered set of milestones (respecting the dependency DAG, leaf crates first) each with an explicit done-check, rather than one undifferentiated push.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With ~1,390 tests across 100 binaries and strong inter-crate dependencies, order determines whether progress compounds or stalls; a downstream crate cannot be verified until its dependencies compile and pass. Milestone structure is the only way to keep a task this large tractable.

anchors.0: No plan; edits arbitrary crates in arbitrary order; attempts everything at once.
anchors.3: Vague intent to 'do the crates'; no explicit ordering by dependency; no per-milestone completion criteria.
anchors.5: Follows the suggested leaf-first order (common → storage → api-server → …) with per-crate 'compiles + its tests pass' as the milestone check.
anchors.8: Explicit dependency-aware milestone plan for all ten crates with concrete exit criteria per crate, sub-milestones inside large crates (e.g. api-server: types→storage wiring→handlers→watches), and gating each layer on the prior layer being green.
anchors.10: A living, hierarchical plan that sequences work to maximize compounding progress, isolates high-risk crates early, decomposes each large crate into independently verifiable units with crisp done-checks, and is continually re-ordered as dependency realities and test-failure clusters reveal the true critical path.

dimensions.name: Incremental & semantic verification
dimensions.description: Deliberately using cargo build/test per-crate and workspace-wide, plus reasoning about the hidden conformance suite, to confirm correctness rather than assuming it.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Grading is pass/fail on every non-skipped provided test AND a hidden HTTP conformance suite; self-written tests don't count. The agent must verify continuously against the provided suites while also engineering for real k8s semantics it cannot see — a verification challenge beyond just running the given tests.

anchors.0: Never builds or runs tests; declares crates done by inspection.
anchors.3: Runs cargo build/test only sporadically or only at the very end, so failures pile up undiagnosed.
anchors.5: Builds and runs each crate's provided tests as it goes and the workspace suite periodically, treating a green provided suite as the bar.
anchors.8: Tight verify loop per milestone (build → targeted crate tests → workspace --no-fail-fast), tracks exact pass/fail counts, and deliberately reasons about conformance behavior not covered by visible fixtures (booting the all-in-one binary, checking HTTP/JSON semantics) so it doesn't just fixture-fit.
anchors.10: A rigorous, layered verification regime: fast per-unit checks feeding workspace-wide runs with the prescribed thread/skip settings, systematic triage of failure clusters, AND independent semantic checks against the upstream reference to guard the hidden conformance suite — catching over-fitting that would pass visible tests yet fail conformance.

dimensions.name: Test-count & horizon tracking
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which crates/tests pass vs. remain across ~1,390 tests, and detecting stuck/circular states rather than losing the plot.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The horizon is enormous; without an accurate running tally of done-vs-remaining and detection of thrashing (re-debugging the same crate, regressions in already-green crates), the agent will lose orientation, repeat work, or quit while wrongly believing it is close.

anchors.0: No sense of overall progress; cannot say which crates pass or how many tests remain.
anchors.3: Rough qualitative sense ('common seems done'); doesn't notice regressions or repeated failures.
anchors.5: Tracks per-crate pass/fail status and roughly how much of the suite is green; notices when a crate is stuck.
anchors.8: Maintains a concrete, updated ledger of pass counts per test binary and remaining work, watches for regressions in previously-green crates after downstream edits, and flags when it is looping on the same failure.
anchors.10: Continuous, accurate accounting across the full 100-binary horizon: distinguishes real forward progress from churn, detects circular debugging early and names it, and reprioritizes based on where the largest verified gains remain — never mistaking local activity for global progress.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising the implementation approach, inferred contract, or crate ordering when build/test evidence contradicts expectations, instead of barrelling ahead.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Many contracts are inferred and will be wrong; some crates will prove harder or more entangled than expected. The ability to abandon a falsified API assumption or resequence when a dependency blocks progress is what separates sustained progress from thrashing on a dead approach.

anchors.0: Repeats the same failing approach unchanged despite persistent errors; never revisits assumptions.
anchors.3: Makes only local patch-the-error fixes; doesn't reconsider a wrong contract or bad ordering even when failures cluster.
anchors.5: When a test reveals a wrong signature/field/semantic, updates the implementation and adjusts nearby work accordingly.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a whole approach or inferred contract is wrong (not just a typo), backs out and reworks it, and reorders remaining crates when a dependency proves blocking — citing the test/reference evidence that triggered the change.
anchors.10: Fluid, evidence-driven adaptation across the horizon: detects systemic mistakes early, cleanly abandons falsified designs before sinking more cost, revises the plan and re-verifies affected downstream crates, and consistently converts contradictory evidence into a better model rather than defending the original path.
